builder_plan.scenario: Start with one repeated product task that has a measurable failure or cost.
builder_plan.change: Read the methods and identify one change you can isolate in that workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current implementation on the same held-out tasks.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful outcomes, response time, human rework, and total cost per successful task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Engineering Low-Latency, High-Throughput Quantum Decoders on NVIDIA GPUs
summary: The method replaces CPU-based or unoptimized GPU quantum error correction decoders with a CUDA-Graph-driven Relay belief-propagation decoder using mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic, INT8 quantization, and concurrent decoder instances. It costs substantial CUDA engineering effort, quantization accuracy risk mitigated by higher-precision accumulators, and workload-specific tuning per code family. It can fail if quantization degrades logical error rates on untested codes or error regimes, and it is irrelevant unless the adopter operates quantum error correction workloads.
rationale: The technique targets quantum error correction decoding, a specialized hardware-software problem outside the production scope of an AI/ML engineer serving conventional models.

claims.statement: The method replaces CPU-based or unoptimized GPU quantum error correction decoders with a CUDA-Graph-driven Relay belief-propagation decoder using mixed FP16-FP32 arithmetic, INT8 quantization, and concurrent decoder instances. It costs substantial CUDA engineering effort, quantization accuracy risk mitigated by higher-precision accumulators, and workload-specific tuning per code family. It can fail if quantization degrades logical error rates on untested codes or error regimes, and it is irrelevant unless the adopter operates quantum error correction workloads.

On the bivariate bicycle code at error probability 0.003, INT8 halves amortized decoding time relative to independently tuned FP32 on an RTX 5080, and an RTX 5080 delivers 91% of GH200 peak throughput with 8.9x shorter median submission-to-correction latency.
